acceptanceCriteria: One command takes a committed branch plus a citation plan from BASE to a sealed, checked tree; its tests cover each existing refusal stopping the loop; docs/DOGFOOD.md §4 names it as the default path.
body:
Observed cost. Every lane this week ran the same sequence by hand: pass-0 `dogfood change` to learn hunk IDs, write cites.tsv, `/bin/rm -f .corvint/change.cem.json`, rerun with DOGFOOD_CITATIONS, commit 'chore: bind change evidence', rerun, `make dogfood-check`, `make dogfood-seal`, push. Each step has its own refusal class (invalid-requirements-section, citation-plan-not-provided, citation-plan-uniform, record-index-failed 'commit the sidecar', DIRTY_WORKTREE) and the recovery for each is held in agent memory, not in the tool. A lane spends roughly a third of its wall clock on this loop and the Codex round; the recipe is identical every time.

Expected: a single command (or `make dogfood-finish BASE=<sha> CITATIONS=<tsv>`) that runs the loop end to end, stops at the first refusal with the existing `fix:` line, makes the bind and seal commits itself, and leaves the pushed state for the PR; the per-step commands stay for repair. Keep every NOT_PRODUCED reason visible in one report.
Actual: six manual steps, each with a memorised recovery.

Version: origin/main 88197e465 (2026-10-13). Source: SDD review by the orchestrating session for decisions 0523/0525 after PRs #850..#855.
title: dogfood: one `corvint dogfood finish-lane` recipe (citations → bind commit → recheck → seal → push) to replace the six-step manual bind loop every lane repeats
